ledger.claim: The rider is not carrying the disputed charge. The fare breakdown records the 6.50 SGD as already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 6.50), and the trip record shows the same reversal at 17:00:40 ('refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review'). POL-GEN-03 defines NO_ACTION as the filing party's claim not being supported and the present state standing, and says in terms that NO_ACTION 'never means restore a charge'. The driver's filing asks for exactly that restoration - his compensation back - and this trip's record supplies him no positive entitlement that the interim reversal displaced, so the present state must stand.

The driver asks for the whole 6.50 SGD back as 'my compensation', but that sum is not the fee this policy fixes. POL-NS-22 transfers to the driver, as compensation for time and fuel, a no-show cancellation fee of 5.00 SGD, and POL-NS-26 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD. The fare breakdown's own money block reports fee_matches_policy false, with policy_fee_sgd 5.00 against fee_charged_sgd 6.50, and the rider's own statement objects to precisely that excess ('more than the $5 I know about'). The 1.50 SGD above the policy fee is an amount the policy does not authorise as a fee at all, so it cannot be compensation for the driver's time and fuel and cannot be moved back to him; POL-NS-22's prescribed handling of a charge that is not 5.00 SGD is a referral naming that clause, which records the amount error rather than validating it.

If the Judge is not satisfied that this record establishes the rider's non-appearance, the case belongs with a human. The only trace in the case is the driver's own device trace: its rider track is empty and it carries no rider-side data at all, so on the fact a no-show charge presupposes - that the rider was not at the pickup - the record offers only the driver's side. POL-GEN-26 provides that where a fact a rule of this version needs cannot be established on the evidence, the case is escalated and the open question stated, with no outcome inferred from the absence; and an escalated fee is held rather than collected, so the rider's refund should not be disturbed while that question is answered.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met, not breached. Before cancelling the trip at 14:15:40 he sent two in-app chat messages to the rider (14:09:40 and 14:13:00, both delivered and read) and placed an in-app call at 14:12:10, so both limbs of the rule - at least one in-app message AND at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at - are satisfied. The FULL_REFUND that POL-NS-23 licenses where either limb is missing therefore does not arise on this record.

The driver complied with the free wait required by POL-NS-21. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so the free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 14:09:15; the 300 s wait expired at 14:14:15 and the driver cancelled at 14:15:40, 385 s after the wait started. The cancellation therefore came after the free wait, which is the precondition POL-NS-22 sets for a no-show fee at all.

The driver's arrival at the pickup is corroborated by the GPS trace on the category's arrival test: the nearest fix (14:09:55) is 2.89 m from the recorded pickup point, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone and inside the 25 m GPS accuracy filter, with an accuracy of 4 m reported. The pre-pass records arrival_check.corroborated as true, so the arrival event at 14:09:15 is not a bare button press.

The rider-side remedy in POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) is not triggered. That clause refunds the fee only where the driver failed to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes; here the driver accepted at 14:02:55 and was at the pickup at 14:09:15, and the GPS trace shows him stationary at the pickup from 14:09:25 through 14:15:25. Nothing in POL-NS-24 obliges a refund or the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit on these facts.

The no-show fee was validly earned and must stand, which under POL-NS-22 means DRIVER_COMPENSATION to the driver. Every precondition is on the record: the driver arrived, waited out the free wait, contacted the rider by message and by call before cancelling, and cancelled as RIDER_NO_SHOW. POL-NS-22 provides that where the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with both amount fields equal to the fee charged, and POL-GEN-03 confirms the driver is owed that money.

The amount the record charged (6.50 SGD) is above the 5.00 SGD figure in POL-NS-22, and the clause's own answer is a referral, not a voiding of the fee: where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause. So the mismatch the rider raises in their statement is a referral point only, and the money the driver claims is the 6.50 SGD actually charged and actually reversed out of his account.

The rider's own filed statement does not deny the no-show; it accepts the charge was a no-show charge and objects only that 6.50 SGD exceeds the 5.00 SGD they knew of. The no-show itself is therefore common ground, and the only rider-side objection is the amount, which POL-NS-22 resolves by acting on the amount charged with a referral rather than by returning the fee.

NO_ACTION would be a loss for the driver and must not be the ruling. The fare ledger shows payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd of 6.50, and the trip record shows the fee was refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver at 17:00:40 after the rider's complaint. NO_ACTION preserves that present state, so on a driver-filed dispute it leaves the driver unpaid for a no-show he lawfully completed; the driver's claim is for the 6.50 SGD to be returned TO HIM, which is DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-GEN-03.

No fact the no-show rules need is unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation. The artifacts the no-show rules require - the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown - are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The only absent artifact is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05060-01, which is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it is disclosed as impaired, and no clause of the no-show policy requires traffic data, so its absence leaves no open question for a human reviewer.

The AI may decide this dispute on the money. The amount contested is 6.50 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band at which POL-GEN-22 requires a minimum confidence, and both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, so the 0.95 fraud-flag bar does not apply and no safety indicator is on the record. POL-NS-26 likewise makes the AI ruling final on a no-show subject to those two bars, neither of which is engaged.

ruling.explanation:
Outcome: the no-show fee stands, and the 6.50 SGD refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver is to be paid back to the driver, so the driver receives 6.50 SGD (DRIVER_COMPENSATION; amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd carry the same figure, 6.50).

To the driver: every no-show condition is on the record. The trip was on-demand with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from your arrival at 14:09:15 and expired at 14:14:15; you cancelled at 14:15:40, after it. Your arrival is corroborated on the category's arrival test — the nearest GPS fix (14:09:55) is 2.89 m from the recorded pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter, with 4 m accuracy reported. Under POL-NS-23 you sent two in-app messages (14:09:40 and 14:13:00) and placed an in-app call (14:12:10), all before the 14:15:40 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met and no FULL_REFUND arises under that clause. The trace also shows you stationary at the pickup from 14:09:25 to 14:15:25, so POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) is not triggered — you did arrive — and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due.

To the rider: your objection is the amount — you were charged 6.50 SGD, not the 5.00 SGD the policy fixes — and that is correct on the record: the fare breakdown reports fee_matches_policy false, with policy_fee_sgd 5.00 against fee_charged_sgd 6.50. But POL-NS-22's own answer to a charge other than 5.00 SGD is to rule on the amount charged and add a referral; it does not void the fee, and POL-NS-26 fixes the fee without making an amount error a ground for refunding it. The referral above sends the 6.50-versus-5.00 discrepancy for review. The no-show itself is not denied on this record: the platform's wait timer expired with the rider not on board, the driver's call went unanswered, and your own statement accepts the charge was a no-show charge.

On the escalation argument under POL-GEN-26: no rule here needs a rider-side trace. The facts the no-show rules require — arrival, the free wait, contact before cancelling, and the fee charged — are carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (trip record EV-TRIP-05060, GPS trace EV-GPS-05060, chat log EV-CHAT-05060, fare breakdown EV-FARE-05060). The only absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05060-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact and is not required by any no-show rule, so its absence leaves no open question and no ground to hold the fee.

The deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The dispute value is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both fraud_flags 0), so no minimum confidence applies (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26); no safety indicator is present (POL-GEN-21). No referral arises under POL-NS-24 (no goodwill credit) or POL-NS-25 (the repeat no-show counter is not present on the rider profile).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-22: refer the fee-amount discrepancy — the record charged 6.50 SGD where POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD — for review; the money ruling acts on the amount actually charged.
